name: NY-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+24 partisan lean makes a Republican win extremely unlikely
Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, has raised $17.5 million and holds $4.4 million on hand
Republican challenger Lewis Mizrahi shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 98%
model.rationale: The district's D+24 lean, Jeffries' national profile and overwhelming financial advantage, and a challenger with no visible resources all point to a decisive Democratic win, and markets agree at roughly 98%. Nothing in the evidence suggests meaningful risk to the incumbent.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or outside spending would be the only plausible signal of a closer race, though even that would be unlikely to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hakeem Jeffries, the House Democratic leader, seeks another term in a Brooklyn-based district with a D+24 partisan lean. He has raised $17.5 million and holds $4.4 million on hand, while Republican challenger Lewis Mizrahi reports no fundraising and draws no outside support. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98 percent.

No general-election polls are available for this race, but the fundamentals leave little ambiguity: the incumbent's incumbency, national stature, and financial dominance sit atop a district that has been solidly Democratic. The forecast calls for a comfortable Jeffries victory, with the only uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
